I just barely recommend this game, like a 6.5/10 rating.  It's not bad, it's not great, right there in the middle.

The plot is basic enough and fairly standard for life management VNs like this: you go to school and manage clubs, helping the girls out to increase your affection with them.  The girls are each different and interesting, you'll probably find at least one you like.  I found the writing to be actually very funny and clever, which was unexpected.  There were a fair amount of typos and grammar issues, which is always aggravating for a VN - the whole purpose of which is reading.  I can't believe developers can't be bothered with proofreading. 

There is no voice acting and not many sound effects.  The music was catchy and it didn't annoy me after several play-throughs, which is a plus.  The artwork was well done, both backgrounds and characters.  No motion or animations, just still images.  The 18+ patch was pretty good, but it's a pain to get it now.

The biggest problem is the game play; you could cut the amount of activities in half, or halve the timeline, and it would still feel like a tedious slog.  It really needed to be streamlined.  The concept is good and I enjoyed increasing stats to meet goals, but geez it just goes on forever.  Seriously, so much time passed between events with the girls, doing a billion mind-numbing clicks, that I forgot what was going on and had to pause to remind myself.  And then at the end of the game, the girl's story wraps up and you finish your responsibilities, but they still have you increasing stats uselessly just to end the year!  The positive is, you get really good at clicking really fast through muscle memory just to skip through it.

The achievements are a bit ridiculous.  Half make sense and can be achieved through the stories or careful stat planning, but then the other half are just outrageous filler, requiring half a dozen play-throughs doing one achievement each (hint: it's real easy to cheat thru them, see the guides).

Overall, I enjoyed interacting with the girls and seeing their stories a lot, however, the game play was just tedious.  If you like these kind of VNs, then I do recommend it.

Of note: I bought and started playing this without realizing it's part of a larger series of games.  It's like a disconnected side story to the rest.  There were quite a few references and easter eggs throughout the game, but they were so obviously broadcast, that even I knew they meant something.  I'll probably check those games out, maybe it'll make me like this one more.  Shrug.

[h1]Sunrider Academy: Donde tus sueños de gestionar chicas se vuelven realidad... casi[/h1]

[h2]Resumen[/h2]
En el mundo de videojuegos poco ortodoxos llega Sunrider Academy, donde simulación, gestión y un poquito de romance se dan la mano, se tropiezan y a veces se caen. Súbete al tren de emociones de ser hermano mayor y presidente de medio instituto mientras tratas de mantener tu cordura y tu vida social en pie.

[h2]Aspectos importantes e interesantes[/h2]
Sunrider Academy te pone en los zapatos de Kayto Shields, un tipo con demasiada responsabilidad sobre sus hombros. No solo intentas mantener tus notas y vida social a flote, sino que también te conviertes en el presidente de unos cuantos clubes escolares. ¿La parte divertida? Intentar que los clubes no fracasen miserablemente mientras intentas no fracasar tú mismo en la vida amorosa. Navega calendarios, gestiona recursos y haz malabares socorriendo cada situación de crisis en tu academia.

[h2]Aspectos por mejorar[/h2]
Las mecánicas de gestión a veces sienten como llenar un Excel sin la satisfacción de un trabajo bien hecho pagado a fin de mes, y pueden volverse algo repetitivas. Aunque la personalización y las interacciones con los personajes son divertidas, en ocasiones los diálogos pueden ser tan densos que ni una taza de café te mantiene despierto.

Entertaining VN at its base and the characters are interesting enough... but there's dialogue scenes that refer to events that have already happened (such as one character telling me I need to study to pass the exam.... and the exam was several days before that I passed). So that's poor coding in checking before that scene runs.

The worst coding, however, is in the time management system. It's a tedium of repetitive clicking, and there's a lot to keep track of in terms of juggling statistics and remembering what you did when. It takes too long and it's not fun. Further, the stats required to have success are completely unclear and obfuscated, so you're having to guess unless you go look at a guide where some kind, helpful person has figured out the formulas and given you a rough idea of what metrics to shoot for at any given point.

This is absolutely not worth it at the full price point. At $2.50 (its current sale price), sure. But then do one or both of: 1) Look up a guide to get a sense of what you're supposed to do when; 2) enable and use the console cheat commands to eliminate as much of the time management hassles as possible.

It's too bad - had this been done as a VN-first; time management lite (or at least coherent!), this would be one to recommend. But this game is thoughtlessly designed and buries its strengths in a mound of busywork that finds its in-game symbolism in the endless paperwork that gets referenced.

*****NOTE*****
